title: Determine Whether Two Positive Integer Numbers Are Coprime
required_features: A sound, built-in integer divisibility or greatest-common-divisor predicate whose semantics are linked to OCaml int inputs.
Refinement support sufficient to state gcd(a,b)=1 exactly (for example, divisibility plus quantification over positive common divisors, or a verified built-in gcd relation).
If a GCD primitive is exposed to synthesis, a checked contract proving that primitive's relationship to divisibility; an opaque declaration is insufficient.
semantic_obligations: Accept only positive inputs under the authoritative precondition a > 0 and b > 0.
Return true if and only if the mathematical gcd of the two inputs is 1.
Return false exactly when the positive inputs have a common divisor greater than 1.
Match the official examples: coprime 13 27 = true and coprime 20536 7826 = false.
Do not invent behavior for zero or negative inputs.

synquid_runtime_evidence.runtime: Synquid v0.4, 2016-08-11 in the supplied pinned rootfs
synquid_runtime_evidence.logic_evidence: src/Synquid/Logic.hs defines arithmetic refinement operators Times, Plus, and Minus and comparisons, but no integer division or modulus operator; src/Synquid/Tokens.hs likewise exposes no div/mod token. The formula grammar has no existential quantifier syntax.

decision: No contract.sq was emitted and no synthesis was attempted. Any available approximation based only on examples, a bounded grid, or an opaque gcd declaration would be weaker than the required iff relationship and is therefore rejected.
